definition: An interactive sport is a sport in which performance and play are continually shaped by the actions of multiple players and by changing game conditions. Because many factors influence each other during play, understanding it requires attention to context and player interaction.

reasons: The packet supports that handball is described as a “collective, complex, dynamic, and interactive sport” and that performance analysis should take into account “context and interaction between different factors and variables,” but it does not explicitly support the definition’s claims that performance and play are “continually shaped” by “multiple players,” or that this is due to “changing game conditions.”

The definition’s wording goes beyond the packet by generalizing from the handball example to an abstract account of how play is shaped and why, without the packet providing explicit statements for those exact mechanisms or terms.

The definition adds unsupported specifics such as “multiple players” and “changing game conditions”; the packet only says handball is a collective, complex, dynamic, and interactive sport that requires attention to context and interaction among factors and variables.
